captive_summary: SPLIT FINDING — shore side is a documented direction-test NO, but the vessel side is undocumented, and per the fuel gate (unstated fuel = INSUFFICIENT, never NO) the terminal verdict is INSUFFICIENT. Shore side (green): the Hadera FSRU (Excelsior, 2013-2022; a submerged-buoy deepwater mooring, Israel's first LNG import point) fed regasified gas into Israel Natural Gas Lines' (INGL) national transmission grid, which in turn supplies gas to essentially all of Israel's major power stations (~70% of national generation), not a single dedicated on-site plant. IEC's own Orot Rabin station (Hadera) is one of the grid's largest offtakers and converted from coal to GE 9HA gas turbines on this same gas supply. Regasification heat itself is met by boiler steam (closed loop) or seawater (open loop) — thermal, not electric, per the heat-is-not-power rule, so it would not count as captive power even setting the direction test aside.
confirmed_how: Georgetown Journal of International Affairs (2020): INGL's ~700 km transmission system 'supply[ies] high-pressure natural gas to major consumers such as electric power generators,' with gas from Hadera entering this shared grid in 2013; Global Energy Observatory's Hadera Deepwater LNG Terminal entry corroborates the buoy/grid-injection design; GE Vernova's Israel Electric Orot Rabin case study confirms IEC's Hadera-area Orot Rabin plant runs on this national gas supply via its own GE 9HA conversion, i.e. Orot Rabin is a grid offtaker of common-carrier gas, not a captive plant built to serve the terminal. VESSEL SIDE (the open half): Riviera documents the Energy Bridge class design as carrying 'an oversize boiler to provide the steam and power necessary to sustain vessel operations and the shipboard regasification process' — the Excelsior self-powers via its steam plant — but no source found states what fuel that plant burns (BOG/dual-fuel vs. fuel oil), so the fuel gate blocks both YES and NO on the vessel half.

status_or_other_findings: Excelsior FSRU left Hadera in December 2022 (charter not renewed) and was redeployed, ultimately serving Germany's Wilhelmshaven terminal from 2025; GEM's 'idled/actual' status is consistent with the terminal being currently unserved rather than decommissioned.
notes: ORCHESTRATOR QC OVERTURN (2026-08-01): researcher returned NO (green) on the direction test alone while explicitly unable to confirm the Excelsior's own onboard generation fuel. Batch convention treats the FSRU's onboard plant as the captive question (Aqaba, Khor Al-Zubair, Mina Al-Ahmadi all YES on documented onboard gas-burning generation), and the fuel gate says unstated fuel = INSUFFICIENT, never NO — so the terminal verdict becomes INSUFFICIENT with the shore-side direction-test NO preserved above. Shore half stands: Hadera's purpose was injecting import gas into the national grid feeding Orot Rabin and other IEC/private stations — a PowerPlantsSupplied relationship for a different batch, never CaptiveGasPower. Vessel half open: could not confirm whether the Excelsior's hotel/auxiliary load (pumps/vaporizers) is generated via turbo-generators off dual-fuel boilers (Kawasaki UA-360 steam turbine confirmed for main propulsion) or diesel gensets. Sources attempted without a fuel statement: 4 vessel databases (researcher), q88 (redirect dead-end), Riviera FSRU-familiarity article (documents the class's oversize self-powering boiler, fuel unstated), Wartsila encyclopedia LNG RV entry, aukevisser Exmar RV spec page (36,000 SHP steam turbine, no genset/fuel data); OTC-18398 ('The Development of the First Energy Bridge Regasification Vessel', OnePetro) is paywalled and is the likeliest place the fuel spec is published — worth a library pull if this row is revisited. Steam-LNG-carrier boilers customarily burn BOG, but that is class-level inference, which this workflow prohibits as a basis for YES.

captive_summary: Proposed FLNG project (Leviathan Phase 1B) for the offshore, moored-vessel Leviathan field, ~130 km off Haifa. NewMed/Chevron 'confirmed the design concept' and funded pre-FEED work in 2023 (targeting a Golar-chartered vessel, described only as a 'generic mark III newbuild solution up to 5mtpa'), but the project remains pre-FID as of this research (August 2026) with no publicly disclosed generation-system specifics. A January 2026 Chevron/NewMed FID was for expanding Leviathan's platform production capacity to serve the Israel-Egypt pipeline gas deal, NOT for the FLNG facility itself — the standalone FLNG project appears to still be in limbo.
confirmed_how: LNG Prime (2023) and Energy Voice (2023, Wayback-verified) both report the design-concept confirmation and pre-FEED budget approval without generation-system detail; MEES (Jan 2026) confirms the subsequent FID covered platform production expansion for pipeline export via the Israel-Egypt deal, not the FLNG facility. No source found (independent or otherwise) describes power-generation equipment for this specific project; as a moored offshore FLNG vessel with no grid access it would, by class norm, require self-generation (all built Golar FLNG units — Hilli Episeyo, Gimi, Fuji — use Baker Hughes LM2500-family gas turbines), but that is a class-level prior, not a documented finding tied to this specific, still-undesigned vessel.

As a moored, off-grid facility it would necessarily have been designed with on-site power generation, but that generic engineering necessity is not the same as a documented finding for this specific vessel's design.

captive_summary: Direction-test NO: Beddawi was one of Lebanon's Ministry of Energy and Water's planned FSRUs (2013 World Bank concept: located 1.7 km off Beddawi, ~3.5 mtpa), explicitly designed as import/regasification/storage infrastructure that pipes gas ~2.5 km to a gas terminal feeding the existing Beddawi/Deir Ammar power complex (465 MW at the time, plus planned expansions), and via the wider coastal 'Gasyle 2' pipeline to other Lebanese power stations. The FSRU itself carries no generation package in any source found — its whole function is fuel supply to power plants it does not own or co-locate with as a captive asset.
confirmed_how: The Edge Malaysia (Petronas shortlist article): describes all three original Ministry FSRUs (Beddawi, Selaata, Zahrani) as vessels where LNG 'is re-converted into gas and piped to power plants and other users' — explicitly a fuel-supply, not generation, function; MEES (2019, 'Lebanon Power Overhaul Gathers Pace'): confirms the Energy Ministry's FSRUs were built 'to supply gas to the grid' via a shared coastal pipeline network feeding multiple CCGT plants, 'rather than each FSRU having dedicated generation capacity.'
